“If one part of the body suffers, every part suffers along with it; and if one part is given glory, every part shares its joy.”
So when one part is given glory, the other parts share its joy; and when it suffers, all the parts suffer. In a body whose parts agree like this, there is no antichrist.

But some people are inside the body of our Lord Jesus Christ in a different way. His body is still being healed, and it will not be perfectly healthy until the resurrection of the dead. These people are in Christ’s body the way bad fluids are in a sick body.
When the body vomits them up, it feels better. In the same way, when bad people leave, the Church feels relief.
And when the body vomits and throws them out, a person says, “These fluids came out of me, but they were not really part of me.”
How were they not part of me?
They were not cut out of my flesh. They just weighed on my chest while they were in me.
5. “They went out from us, but”—don’t be sad—“they were not truly part of us.”
How can you prove this?
If they had been part of us, they would surely have stayed with us.

So you can see from this that many people who are not part of us still receive the sacraments with us. They receive baptism with us. They receive with us what the faithful know they receive: the blessing, the Eucharist, and everything in the holy sacraments. They even share in the very altar with us—and yet they are not part of us.
Temptation proves that they are not part of us.
When temptation comes, they are blown away as if by the wind, because they were never grain.
And as we must often tell you, all of them will be blown away when the Lord begins to separate the grain from the chaff on His threshing floor on the day of judgment.
“They went out from us, but they were not truly part of us. If they had been part of us, they would surely have stayed with us.”
Do you want to know, dear friends, how very certain this saying is? Those who may have gone out but then come back are not antichrists. They are not against Christ.
Those who are not antichrists cannot possibly stay outside.
But each person chooses for himself whether to be an antichrist or to be in Christ.
Either we are among the parts of the body, or among the bad fluids.
Whoever changes for the better is in the body, as one of its parts. But whoever stays in his wickedness is a bad fluid. And when he has gone out, those who were weighed down by him will feel relief.

“They went out from us, but they were not truly part of us. If they had been part of us, they would surely have stayed with us. But they went out so that it would become clear that not all of them were part of us.”
He added the words “so that it would become clear” because even while they are inside, they are not part of us. But it isn’t clear then. It only becomes clear when they go out.
“And you have an anointing from the Holy One, so that you can be seen clearly by your own selves.”
The spiritual anointing is the Holy Spirit Himself. The visible anointing is the sacrament—the outward sign—of this.
He says that everyone who has this anointing of Christ can tell the bad from the good. They don’t need to be taught, because the anointing itself teaches them.
6. “I am writing to you, not because you don’t know the truth, but because you do know it, and you know that no lie comes from the truth.”
Look—here we are shown how to recognize the antichrist.
What is Christ? The Truth.
He Himself said, “I am the Truth.”
But “no lie comes from the truth.”
So everyone who lies does not yet belong to Christ.
He did not say that some lies come from the truth and some lies don’t.
Pay attention to these words. Don’t pamper yourselves. Don’t flatter yourselves. Don’t fool yourselves. Don’t cheat yourselves. “No lie comes from the truth.”
So let’s see how the antichrists lie, because there is more than one kind of lying.
“Who is a liar? Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ.”
The word “Jesus” means one thing, and the word “Christ” means another. There is only one Jesus Christ our Savior, but “Jesus” is His personal name.
Moses was called by his personal name, and so were Elijah and Abraham. In the same way, our Lord has “Jesus” as His personal name. But “Christ” is the name of His holy office.
It is like when we say “Prophet” or “Priest.” The name “Christ” tells us that He is the Anointed One, through whom the whole people would be rescued.
The Jewish people were hoping for this Christ to come. But because He came humbly, they did not recognize Him. The stone was small, so they tripped over it and were broken.
But “the stone grew and became a great mountain.” And what does Scripture say?
“Whoever trips over this stone will be broken, and anyone this stone comes down on will be crushed to powder.”
We need to notice the difference in the words. It says whoever trips will be broken, but whoever it comes down on will be crushed to powder.
At first, people tripped over Him because He came humbly. But He will come in greatness to judge, and He will crush to powder anyone He comes down on.
But when He comes in the future, He will not crush anyone whom He did not break when He first came.
Whoever did not trip over the humble Christ will not need to fear the glorious Christ.
You have heard it in a few words, brothers and sisters: whoever did not trip over the humble Christ will not need to fear the glorious Christ.
For Christ is a stumbling stone to all bad people. Everything Christ says tastes bitter to them.
7. So listen and see.

All who go out from the Church and are cut off from the Church’s unity are certainly antichrists. No one should doubt it. The apostle himself pointed them out: “They went out from us, but they were not truly part of us. If they had been part of us, they would surely have stayed with us.”
So those who do not stay with us but go out from us are clearly antichrists.
And how can we prove that they are antichrists?
By their lying. “And who is a liar? Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ.”
Let’s question the heretics. Where will you find a heretic who denies that Jesus is the Christ?
Look now, my dear friends—here is a great mystery.
Notice what the Lord God may have inspired in us, and what I would love to plant in your minds.
Look: they went out from us and became Donatists. We ask them whether Jesus is the Christ, and right away they declare that Jesus is the Christ.

So if an antichrist is someone who denies that Jesus is the Christ, then they can’t call us antichrists, and we can’t call them that either. That would mean they did not go out from us, and we did not go out from them.

And if we have not gone out from each other, then we are united. But if we are united, why are there two altars in this city? Why are there divided households and divided marriages? Why do husband and wife share one bed but have a divided Christ?
He is warning us. He wants us to admit the truth: either they went out from us, or we went out from them.
But no one should imagine that we went out from them.
We have the Lord’s will, which names His inheritance. We read it aloud, and there we find: “I will give You the nations as Your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as Your possession.”
We hold on to Christ’s inheritance. They do not, because they are not in fellowship with the whole world. They are not in fellowship with the worldwide body that was bought back by the Lord’s blood.

We have the Lord Himself, risen from the dead, who let His doubting disciples touch Him with their hands. While they were still doubting, He said to them, “Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, and repentance and forgiveness of sins had to be preached in His name”—Where? In which direction? To whom?—“to all nations, starting from Jerusalem.”
Our minds are at peace about the unity of the inheritance!
Whoever is not in fellowship with this inheritance has gone out.
8. But let’s not be sad: “They went out from us, but they were not truly part of us. If they had been part of us, they would surely have stayed with us.”
So if they went out from us, they are antichrists. If they are antichrists, they are liars. If they are liars, they deny that Jesus is the Christ.
Once again we come back to the hard part of the question.
Ask them one at a time, and they all declare that Jesus is the Christ.
The difficulty that holds us back comes from taking the words of the letter in too narrow a way.
Anyway, you see the question. If it isn’t understood, this question leaves both us and them stuck.
Either we are antichrists or they are antichrists. They call us antichrists and say we went out from them. We say the same about them.
But this letter has given us a mark to recognize the antichrists by: “Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ” is “an antichrist.”
So now let’s find out who denies Him. And let’s look not at the tongue, but at the actions.
For if you ask everyone, they will all say with one voice that Jesus is the Christ.
Let the tongue be quiet for a little while. Ask the life instead.

Suppose we find this: suppose Scripture itself tells us that you can deny Christ not only with your words but also with your actions. Then we will certainly find many antichrists. With their mouths they say they believe in Christ, but the way they live disagrees with Christ.
Where do we find this in Scripture?
Listen to Paul the apostle. He says about such people, “They say openly that they know God, but their actions deny Him.”
We find that these people are antichrists too. Anyone who denies Christ by his actions is an antichrist.
I don’t listen to what he says. I look at how he lives.
Actions speak—so do we need words?
After all, what bad person doesn’t want to speak well?
But what does the Lord say to people like that?
“You hypocrites! How can you say good things when you are evil?”
You bring your voices to My ears, but I look into your thoughts.
I see an evil will there, and you are showing off fake fruit.
I know what I should pick, and where to pick it from. I don’t “pick figs from thistles.” I don’t pick “grapes from thorns.” For “every tree is known by its fruit.”
The antichrist who lies even more is the one who says with his mouth that Jesus is the Christ, but denies Him with his actions.
He is a liar because he says one thing and does another.
9. So, brothers and sisters, if we are to judge by actions, we find not only many antichrists who have gone out, but also many who are not yet exposed and have not gone out at all.

The Church has many people inside it who break their oaths, cheat others, practice dark magic, go to fortune-tellers, commit adultery, get drunk, lend money at unfair interest, and kidnap boys—plus all the other sins we can’t even list. All these things go against the teaching of Christ. They go against the word of God.
Now the Word of God is Christ. So whatever goes against the Word of God belongs to the Antichrist.
For “Antichrist” means “against Christ.”
Do you want to know how openly these people resist Christ?

Sometimes they do something evil, and someone begins to correct them. They don’t dare to insult Christ, so they insult His ministers who are correcting them. But if you show them that you are speaking Christ’s words and not your own, they try as hard as they can to prove that you are speaking your own words and not Christ’s. But if it is clear that you are speaking Christ’s words, they go even against Christ. They start to find fault with Christ. “How,” they say, “and why did He make us the way we are?”
Don’t people say this every day when their actions are exposed?
Twisted by a wicked will, they blame their Maker.
Their Maker calls to them from heaven (for the One who made us is the same One who made us new): What did I make you?
I made a human being, not greed. I made a human being, not robbery. I made a human being, not adultery.
You have heard that My works praise Me.
You heard it from the mouths of the Three Young Men—it was that very hymn that protected them from the fire.

The Lord’s works praise the Lord. The heavens, the earth and the sea praise Him. Everything in the heavens praises Him. The angels praise Him, the stars praise Him, the lights praise Him. Whatever swims, whatever flies, whatever walks and whatever crawls praises Him. All these praise the Lord.
Did you hear in that hymn that greed praises the Lord?
Did you hear that drunkenness praises the Lord?
Or that wild living praises Him, or that silliness praises Him?
Whatever you do not hear praising the Lord in that hymn, the Lord did not make.
Fix what you have made, so that what God made in you can be saved.
But if you refuse, and you love and cling to your sins, you are against Christ.
Whether you are inside or outside, you are an antichrist. Whether you are inside or outside, you are chaff.
So why aren’t you outside?
Because no wind has come along yet to blow you away.
10. These things are now clear, my brothers and sisters.
No one should say, “I don’t worship Christ, but I worship God His Father.”
“Everyone who denies the Son has neither the Son nor the Father. And whoever confesses the Son has both the Son and the Father.”
He is speaking to you who are grain. And let those who were chaff listen and become grain.
Each person should look carefully at his own conscience. If he loves the world, he should change. He should become someone who loves Christ, so that he will not be an antichrist.

If someone tells him he is an antichrist, he gets angry. He thinks he has been treated unfairly. And if the person calling him an antichrist is someone he is quarreling with, he may even threaten to take him to court.

Christ says to him: Be patient. If people have said false things about you, be glad with Me, because the antichrists say false things about Me too. But if what they say about you is true, make peace with your own conscience. And if you are afraid of being called this, be even more afraid of being it.
11. “So let what you heard from the beginning stay in you.
If what you heard from the beginning stays in you, you will also stay in the Son and in the Father.
And this is what He has promised us.”

Maybe you will ask about the reward and say: Look, “I keep safe in me what I heard from the beginning. I obey it. To keep holding on, I put up with dangers, hard work and temptations. But what good does it do me? What is my reward? What will He give me later, since in this world I see myself struggling among temptations?

I don’t see any rest here. Just being mortal weighs my soul down, and my body, which decays, drags it down to lower things. But I put up with everything, so that ‘what I heard from the beginning’ will ‘stay’ in me, and so that I can say to my God, ‘Because of the words from Your lips, I have kept to hard roads.’”
So what is the reward?
Listen, and don’t give up.
If you were growing weak in your work, let the promised reward make you strong.
What worker in a vineyard would let the pay he is going to get slip out of his mind?
If he forgot it, his hands would grow weak.
Remembering the promised pay keeps him working steadily. And yet the one who promised it is only a human being, who might let you down.

How much stronger should you be in God’s field! The One who made the promise is the Truth. No one else can ever take His place, He can never die, and He can never deceive the person He made the promise to!
And what is the promise?
Let’s see what He has promised.
Is it gold, which people here love so much? Or silver?
Or property, which people spend their gold on, no matter how much they love gold?
Or beautiful land, big houses, many slaves, lots of animals?
These are not the wages, so to speak, that he urges us to work hard for.
What is this reward called? “Eternal life.”
You heard it, and you shouted for joy. Love what you have heard, and you will be set free from your hard work into the rest of eternal life.
Look, this is what God promises: “eternal life.”
Look, this is what God warns of: eternal fire.
What will He say to those placed on His right?
“Come, you whom My Father has blessed. Take the kingdom made ready for you since the world began.”
And what to those on the left?
“Go into the eternal fire that was prepared for the devil and his angels.”
You don’t love that yet—so at least be afraid of this.
12. So remember, my brothers and sisters, that Christ has promised us eternal life. “This,” he says, “is the promise He has promised us: eternal life.
I have written these things to you about those who are trying to lead you astray.”
Don’t let anyone lead you astray to death. Long for the promise of eternal life.
What can the world promise?
Let it promise whatever you like—it may be making that promise to someone who will die tomorrow.
And how will you dare to face Him who lasts forever when you leave this life?
“But a powerful man is threatening me, to force me to do something evil.”
What does he threaten you with?
Prison, chains, fire, torture, wild animals. Yes—but not eternal fire, is it?
Fear what the One Almighty threatens. Love what the One Almighty promises. Then the whole world will seem worthless to us, whether it makes promises or makes threats.
“I have written these things to you about those who are trying to lead you astray. I want you to know that you have an anointing, and that the anointing we have received from Him should stay in you.”

In the anointing we have the sacramental sign [of something unseen], but its power is invisible. The invisible anointing is the Holy Spirit. The invisible anointing is that love which will be like a root in anyone who has it. No matter how hot the sun gets, he cannot dry up.
Anything that has roots is fed by the sun’s heat, not dried up by it.
13. “You do not need anyone to teach you, because His anointing teaches you about everything.”
Then why do “we” teach you, my brothers and sisters?
If “His anointing teaches you about everything,” it seems we are working for nothing.
And why do we cry out the way we do?
Let us just leave you to His anointing, and let His anointing teach you.

But so far I am only asking myself this question. I also put it to the apostle himself. May he kindly listen to a little child who asks him something. To John himself I say: Did the people you were speaking to have the anointing?
You said, “His anointing teaches you about everything.”
Then why did you write a letter like this? What teaching did “you” give them? What instruction? What building up?
Look at this, brothers and sisters. Look at a great mystery.
The sound of our words hits your ears, but the real Teacher is inside.
Do not think that anyone learns anything from another human being.
We can warn and remind you with the sound of our voice. But if there is not Someone inside who teaches, all our noise is useless.
Yes, brothers and sisters, do you want to know it?
Haven’t you all heard this sermon? And yet how many people will leave here without having learned anything!
I have spoken to everyone. But some people are not spoken to by that Anointing inside them, and the Holy Spirit does not teach them inside. Those people go home without having learned anything.
The lessons of a teacher on the outside are only a kind of help and reminder.
The One who teaches hearts has His teaching chair in heaven.
That is why He Himself says in the Gospel: “Do not call anyone on earth your teacher. You have one Teacher, and that is Christ.”
So let Him speak to you inside, when no human being is there. Someone may be standing beside you, but no one is inside your heart.

Yet do not let your heart be empty. Let Christ be in your heart. Let His anointing be in your heart. Otherwise it will be a heart dying of thirst in the desert, with no springs of water to drink from.
So, I say, there is a Teacher inside who teaches. Christ teaches. His inspiration teaches.
Where His inspiration and His anointing are missing, words just make noise on the outside, and it is useless.

Brothers and sisters, the words we speak from the outside are like a gardener caring for a tree. He works from the outside. He waters it and takes good care of it. But whatever he does from the outside, does he shape the apples? Does he cover the bare branches with shady leaves? Does he do anything like that from the inside?
Then who does it?

Listen to the gardener, the apostle. See what we are, and listen to the Teacher inside: “I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. Neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything. Only the One who gives the growth is: God.”
So this is what we tell you: whether we plant or water, our speaking does not make us anything. Only God, who gives the growth, counts. That is, “His anointing, which teaches you about everything.”
“And it is true, and it does not lie.
Just as it has taught you, stay in it.
And now, little children, stay in Him. Then, when He appears, we can be confident and not be put to shame by Him when He comes.
If you know that He is righteous, then know that everyone who does what is right is born of Him.
Look how great a love the Father has given us: we are called God’s children, and we really are! That is why the world does not know us. It did not know Him, so it does not know us either.
Dear friends, we are God’s children now, but it has not yet been shown what we will be.
We know that when He appears, we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is.
And everyone who has this hope in Him makes himself pure, just as He is pure.
Everyone who sins also does wickedness.
Sin is wickedness. And you know that He appeared in order to take away sin, and there is no sin in Him.
Whoever stays in Him does not sin. Whoever sins has not seen Him and has not known Him.
Little children, do not let anyone lead you astray.
The person who does what is right is righteous, just as He is righteous.
The person who sins belongs to the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning.
This is why the Son of God appeared: to destroy the works of the devil.”
1. You remember, brothers and sisters, that yesterday’s reading stopped at this point: “You do not need anyone to teach you, because the anointing itself teaches you about everything.”

I am sure you remember how we explained this. We who speak to your ears from the outside are like workers caring for a tree from the outside. But we cannot make it grow or shape the fruit. Only the One who made you, rescued you and called you can do that. He lives in you by faith and by the Spirit, and He must speak to you inside. Otherwise all our noisy words are useless.
How can we see that this is true?
From this: many people hear, but not all of them are convinced by what is said. Only those to whom God speaks inside are convinced.
Now the people God speaks to inside are the ones who make room for Him. And the people who make room for God are those who “do not make room for the devil.”
For the devil wants to live in people’s hearts and say things there that can lead them astray.
But what does the Lord Jesus say?
“The ruler of this world is thrown out.”
Thrown out of where? Out of heaven and earth? Out of the whole structure of the world?
No, out of the hearts of those who believe.
Now that the invader has been thrown out, let the Redeemer live inside. For the One who rescued us is the same One who made us.
And now the devil attacks from the outside. He cannot defeat the One who has taken possession of the inside.
He attacks from the outside by throwing all kinds of temptations at us. But the person to whom God speaks inside does not give in to them—the person who has the anointing you have heard about.
2. “And it is true”—that is, this anointing. In other words, the Spirit of the Lord Himself, who teaches people, cannot lie. “And it is not false.
Just as it has taught you, stay in it.
And now, little children, stay in Him. Then when He appears, we can stand boldly before Him and not be put to shame by Him when He comes.”

You see, brothers and sisters, we believe in Jesus, whom we have not seen. He was announced to us by people who saw Him, touched Him and heard the word from His own mouth. They were sent by Him to convince the whole human race that this is true. They did not dare to go on their own.
And where were they sent?
You heard it when the Gospel was read: “Go and preach the Gospel to the whole creation under heaven.”
So the disciples were sent “everywhere.” Signs and wonders proved that they had seen what they talked about.
And we believe in Him, whom we have not seen, and we are waiting for Him to come.
Those who wait for Him by faith will be glad when He comes. But those who have no faith will be ashamed when the thing they do not see now finally comes.
And that shame will not last just one day and then go away. It will not be like the embarrassment people usually feel when they are caught doing something wrong and others laugh at them.
That shame will carry the people who feel it off to the left side, so that they will be told, “Go into the fire that lasts forever, which was prepared for the devil and his angels.”
So let us stay in His words, so that we will not be put to shame when He comes.
For He Himself says in the Gospel to those who had believed in Him: “If you stay in My word, then you really are My disciples.”
And it is as if they had asked, “What good will that do us?”
“And,” He says, “you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
For right now our salvation is something we hope for, not something we already have. We do not yet own what has been promised. We hope for it to come.
And “the One who promised is faithful.” He will not trick you. Just do not give up. Wait for the promise.
For He is the Truth, and He cannot deceive.
Do not be a liar who says one thing and does another. Keep faith, and He will keep His promise.
But if you do not keep faith, you have cheated yourself. It was not the One who promised who cheated you.
3. “If you know that He is righteous, then know that everyone who does what is right is born of Him.”
The righteousness we have right now comes from faith.

Perfect righteousness does not exist except in the angels. And even the angels hardly have it, if you compare them with God. Still, if any souls or spirits that God created are perfectly righteous, it is the angels. They are holy, just and good. No slip has turned them aside. No pride has made them fall. They always keep looking at the Word of God. Nothing else is sweet to them except the One who created them. In them righteousness is perfect. But in us it has only begun, through faith, by the Spirit.
You heard it when the Psalm was read: “Begin with the Lord by confessing.”
“Begin,” it says. Our righteousness begins when we confess our sins.

You have started to stop defending your sin. Now you have made a beginning of righteousness. But it will be made perfect in you when nothing else delights you but this. That will be when “death is swallowed up in victory.” It will be when there is no more itch of desire, and no more struggle with flesh and blood. It will be when the prize of victory is given and the enemy is defeated. Then righteousness will be perfect.
Right now we are still fighting. If we are fighting, we are in the arena. We hit and we get hit. But who will win is still to be seen.
And the one who wins is the person who, even when he lands a blow, does not trust in his own strength. He relies on God, who cheers him on.
When the devil fights against us, he is alone.
If we are with God, we defeat the devil. But if you fight the devil alone, you will be beaten.
He is a skillful enemy. Think how many victories he has won!
Look how far down he has thrown us!
We are born to die because of this: at the very start, he threw our first ancestor out of Paradise.
So what should we do, since he is so experienced?
Call on the Almighty to help you against the devil’s tricks.
Let the One who cannot be beaten live in you. Then you will safely beat the one who usually wins.
But whom does he usually beat?
Those in whom God does not live.

I say this so you will understand, brothers and sisters. When Adam was in Paradise, he ignored God’s command. He stuck his neck up proudly, as if he wanted to be his own master and did not want to obey God’s will. And so he fell from that life without death, from that happiness.

But there was a certain man who had now become very skilled, even though he was born to die. As he sat on the dung heap, rotting with worms, he defeated the devil. Yes, Adam himself won then—in Job! Because Job came from Adam’s family line.
So Adam, who was beaten in Paradise, won on the dung heap.
In Paradise he listened to the woman, who passed on what the devil had put into her mind. But on the dung heap he said to Eve, “You are talking like one of the foolish women.”
There he listened; here he answered back. When he was happy, he listened. When he was beaten with suffering, he won.
So look at what comes next in the letter, my brothers and sisters. This is what it wants us to take to heart: that we really can defeat the devil, but not by our own power.
“If you know that He is righteous,” it says, “then know that everyone who does what is right is born of Him”—born of God, of Christ.
And when he says, “is born of Him,” he is cheering us on.
So already, because we are born of Him, we are perfect.
4. Listen. “Look what great love the Father has given us: that we should be called God’s children, and really be His children.”
For if people are called sons but are not really sons, what good is the name to them when the real thing is missing?
How many people are called doctors who do not know how to heal! How many are called watchmen who sleep all night long!
In the same way, many are called Christians, but their actions show that they are not. They are not what they are called—not in their lives, their behavior, their faith, their hope, or their love.
But what have you heard here, brothers and sisters?

“Look what great love the Father has given us: that we should be called God’s children, and really be His children. That is why the world does not know us. It has not known Him, so it does not know us either.”

There is a whole world of Christians and a whole world of ungodly people. All over the world there are people who do not honor God, and all over the world there are people who do. The first group does not know the second.
In what way do we think they do not know them?
They make fun of people who live good lives.
Pay attention and see. Perhaps there are people like that among you too.

Think of any one of you who now lives for God. He looks down on worldly things. He does not choose to go to the shows. He does not choose to get drunk as if it were a sacred custom. And what is worse, he does not choose to make himself unclean, using holy days as an excuse. The person who refuses to do these things—how the people who do them make fun of him!
Would they laugh at him if they really knew him?
But why do they not know him?
“The world does not know Him.”
Who is “the world”?
The people who live in the world.
It is just like when we say “a house” and mean the people who live in it.
We have told you this again and again, so we will not repeat it and bore you.

By now, when you hear the word “world” used in a bad way, you know it means only those who love the world. Because they love it, they live in it. And because they live in it, they have earned that name.
So the world has not known us, because it has not known Him.
The Lord Jesus Christ Himself walked here in a human body. He was God, but He was hidden in weakness.
And why did people not recognize Him?
Because He pointed out every sin in people.
They loved the pleasures of sin, so they did not recognize God. They loved what their fever made them want, so they mistreated the Doctor.
5. So what about us? What are we?
We are already born of Him. But since we are His children in hope, he says, “Dear friends, we are God’s children now.”
Already, right now? Then what are we waiting for, if we are already God’s children?
“It has not yet been shown,” he says, “what we will be.”
But what else will we be, other than God’s children?
Listen to what comes next: “We know that when He appears, we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is.”
Understand this, my dear friends. It is a great thing: “We know that when He appears, we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is.”
First of all, notice what is called “Is.”
You know what it is that is called by that name.

What is called “Is”—and not only called that, but really is—never changes. It always stays the same. It cannot be changed. No part of It can decay. It does not grow, because It is already perfect. It does not shrink, because It is eternal.
And what is this?
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”
And what is this?
“He was in the form of God, and He did not think it was robbery to be equal with God.”
Bad people cannot see Christ this way—Christ in the form of God, the Word of God, the only Son of the Father, equal with the Father.
But because the Word became flesh, even bad people will be able to see Him. On the day of judgment the bad will see Him too. For He will come to judge in the same form in which He came to be judged.
In that same form He is a man, but still God. For “cursed is everyone who puts his trust in a man.”
As a man He came to be judged. As a man He will come to judge.
And if He will not be seen, what does this Scripture mean: “They will look at Him whom they pierced”?
For it is said about the ungodly that they will see and be put to shame.
How could the ungodly not see, when He puts some on His right side and others on His left?
To those on the right He will say, “Come, you whom My Father has blessed, receive the kingdom.” To those on the left He will say, “Go into the fire that lasts forever.”
They will see only the form of a servant. They will not see the form of God.
Why? Because they were ungodly. And the Lord Himself says, “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.”

So we are going to see a special sight, my brothers and sisters, one “that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has never entered a human heart.” It is a sight more beautiful than anything on earth—more than gold and silver, woods and fields. It is more beautiful than the sea and the sky, than the sun and the moon, than the stars, than the angels. It is greater than everything, because everything gets its beauty from it.
6. So what will “we” be when we see this?
What has been promised to us?
“We will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is.”
My tongue has done what it could. It has spoken the words. Let your heart think about the rest.
For even John himself—what could he say compared with the One who Is? And what can we humans say, when we are so far from being as great as John?
So let us go back to His anointing. Let us go back to the anointing that teaches inside us what we cannot put into words. And since you cannot see it now, your part and your job is to long for it.
The whole life of a good Christian is a holy longing.
Right now you do not yet see what you long for. But by longing, you are made big enough, so that when the thing you will see arrives, you will be filled.

Think of it like this. Suppose you want to fill a bag, and you know how big the thing is that you will be given. So you stretch open the sack or the leather bag or whatever it is. You know how much you want to put in, and you see that the bag is too narrow. By stretching it, you make it able to hold more. In the same way, God makes us wait for what we hope for, and this stretches our longing. The longing stretches our soul. And by stretching it, He makes it bigger.
So let us keep longing, my brothers and sisters, because we will be filled.
Look at Paul. It is as if he is widening his heart so that it can receive what is coming.
This is what he says: “Not that I have already received it or am already perfect. Brothers and sisters, I do not think I have taken hold of it yet.”
Then what are you doing in this life, if you have not taken hold of it yet?
“But I do this one thing: I forget what is behind me and reach out for what is ahead. Straining hard, I keep going toward the prize of the high calling.”
He says he reaches out, or stretches himself. And he says he keeps going “straining hard.”
He felt he was too small to take in the thing “that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has never entered a human heart.”
This is our life: to be trained by longing.
But holy longing trains us only as much as we cut our longings away from loving the world.
We have already said, “Empty out what is going to be filled.”
You are going to be filled with good things, so pour out the bad.
Imagine that God wants to fill you with honey. If you are full of vinegar, where will you put the honey?
What was in the jar must be poured out. The jar itself must be cleaned. It must be cleaned even if it takes hard work and hard scrubbing, so that it is ready for that thing, whatever it is.
We could call it honey, or gold, or wine. Whatever we call it, it is something that cannot be put into words. Whatever we would like to call it, its name is—God.
And when we say “God,” what have we really said?
Is that one syllable all that we are waiting for?
So whatever we have been able to say falls short of Him. Let us stretch ourselves out toward Him, so that when He comes, He may fill us.
For “we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is.”
7. “And everyone who has this hope in Him.”
You see how he has put us in our place: in “hope.”
You see how the apostle Paul agrees with his fellow apostle: “We are saved by hope.
But hope that is seen is not hope. For why would anyone hope for what he already sees?
But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it patiently.”
This patience itself trains our longing.
Keep going, because He stays. Keep on walking so that you reach the goal. The place you are heading for will not move away.
Look: “And everyone who has this hope in Him makes himself pure, just as He is pure.”
See how he has not taken away free will, since he says, “makes himself pure.”
Who makes us pure except God?
Yes, but God does not make you pure if you do not want it.
So when you join your will to God, you make yourself pure.
You make yourself pure—not by your own power, but by the One who comes to live in you.
Still, because you do something in this with your will, some of it is credited to you.
But it is credited to you only so that you will say, as in the Psalm, “Be my helper; do not leave me.”
If you say, “Be my helper,” you are doing something. For if you were doing nothing, how could He be said to “help” you?
8. “Everyone who sins also does wickedness.”
No one should say, “Sin is one thing and wickedness is another.” No one should say, “I am a sinner, but I do not do wickedness.”
For “everyone who sins also does wickedness.
Sin is wickedness.” So then, what should we do about our sins and our wickedness?
Listen to what He says: “And you know that He appeared to take away sin, and there is no sin in Him.”
He, in whom there is no sin, is the One who came to take away sin.
For if there were sin in Him, it would have to be taken away from Him. He could not take it away Himself.
“Whoever stays in Him does not sin.”
As far as he stays in Him, that far he does not sin.
“Whoever sins has not seen Him and has not known Him.”
This is a big question: “Whoever sins has not seen Him and has not known Him.”
No wonder. We have not seen Him, but we are going to see Him. We have not known Him, but we are going to know Him. We believe in Someone we have not known.
Or perhaps we have known Him by faith, but not yet by actually seeing Him?
But then, by faith, we have both seen and known Him.
For if faith does not see yet, why are we said to have been given light?
There is a light that comes by faith, and a light that comes by sight.
Right now, while we are travelers far from home, “we walk by faith, not by sight”—that is, not by actually seeing.
So our righteousness also is “by faith, not by sight.”
Our righteousness will be perfect when we actually see.
But in the meantime, let us not let go of the righteousness that comes by faith. For as the apostle says, “the righteous person lives by faith.”
“Whoever stays in Him does not sin.”
For “whoever sins has not seen Him and has not known Him.”
The person who sins does not believe. But if someone believes, then as far as his faith goes, he does not sin.
9. “Little children, do not let anyone lead you astray.
The person who does what is right is righteous, just as He is righteous.”
What? When we hear that we are “righteous just as He is righteous,” should we think we are equal with God?
You need to understand what “just as” means. He said a little earlier, “makes himself pure, just as He is pure.”
Is our purity then like God’s purity and equal to it? Is our righteousness equal to God’s righteousness?
Who could say that?
But the words “just as” are not always used to mean “equal.”

Here is an example. Suppose someone sees this large church and wants to build a smaller church with the same shape. Say this church is one unit wide and two units long. He builds his church one unit wide and two units long too. Then you can see that he has built it “just as” this one is built.
But say this church is a hundred cubits long and the other one is thirty. It is “just as” this one, and yet it is not equal.
So you see, “just as” does not always mean being the same or equal.

Here is another example. See how different a person’s face is from its reflection in a mirror. There is a face in the reflection, and there is a face on the body. The reflection only copies; the body is the real thing.
And what do we say?
We say that “just as” there are eyes here, so there are eyes there too. “Just as” there are ears here, so there are ears there too.
The things are different, but we say “just as” because they look alike.

In the same way, we also have God’s image in us. But it is not the image that the Son has, who is equal with the Father. Still, if we were not also “just as” He is, in our own measure, we could not be called like Him in any way.
So “He makes us pure, just as He is pure.” But He is pure from all eternity. We are pure by faith.
We are “righteous just as He is righteous.” But He is righteous forever, without ever changing. We are righteous by believing in Someone we do not see, so that one day we may see Him.
Even when our righteousness is made perfect, when we are equal to the angels, even then it will not be equal to Him.
So how far from Him it must be now, if even then it will not be equal!
10. “The person who sins belongs to the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning.”
“Belongs to the devil.” You know what he means: by copying the devil.

For the devil did not make anyone. He did not father anyone. He did not create anyone. But whoever copies the devil becomes a child of the devil, as if the devil had fathered him. He becomes his child by copying him, not by actually being born from him.
In what way are you a child of Abraham, even though Abraham was not your father?
In the same way that the Jews, who were Abraham’s children, became children of the devil by not copying Abraham’s faith. They were born from Abraham’s body, but they did not copy Abraham’s faith.

So those who were born from him were shut out of the inheritance because they did not copy him. But you, who were not born from him, are made his child. And in this way you will be his child: by copying him.
And if you copy the devil—the way he became proud and ungodly against God—you will be a child of the devil. It will be by copying him, not because he created you or fathered you.
11. “This is why the Son of God appeared.”
Now then, brothers and sisters, pay attention!
All sinners are born of the devil, as sinners.
Adam was made by God. But when he gave in to the devil, he was born of the devil. And he fathered all people to be just like himself.
We were born with sinful desire itself. Even before we add our own sins, we are born under that condemnation.
For if we are born without any sin, why do people rush with their babies to baptism to set them free?
So pay close attention, brothers and sisters, to the two family roots, Adam and Christ. There are two men. One is a man who is only man. The other is a Man who is God.
Because of the man who is only man, we are sinners. Through the Man who is God, we are made right with God.
The first birth threw us down into death. The second birth raised us up to life. The first birth brings sin with it. The second birth sets us free from sin.
For this is why Christ came as a Man: to undo people’s sins.
“This is why the Son of God appeared: to undo the works of the devil.”
12. I leave the rest for you to think about, my dear friends, so that I do not wear you out.
For here is the question we are working hard to solve: we call ourselves sinners. For if anyone says he is without sin, he is a liar.
And in the letter of this same John we have found it written, “If we say that we have no sin, we are fooling ourselves.”
For you should remember what came before: “If we say that we have no sin, we are fooling ourselves, and the truth is not in us.”

And yet on the other hand, in what follows you are told, “The one who is born of God does not sin. The one who sins has not seen Him and has not known Him.—Everyone who sins belongs to the devil.” Sin does not come from God. This scares us all over again.
In what way are we born of God, and in what way do we confess that we are sinners?
Should we say it is because we are not born of God?
Then what are these Sacraments doing for babies?
What did John say?
“The one who is born of God does not sin.”
And yet the same John also said, “If we say that we have no sin, we are fooling ourselves, and the truth is not in us!”
It is a big question and a puzzling one. I hope I have made you eager to hear it solved, my dear friends.
Tomorrow, in the Lord’s name, we will talk about it, with whatever He gives us.
“Whoever is born of God does not sin, because his seed stays in him. He cannot sin, because he is born of God.
This is how it becomes clear who are God’s children and who are the devil’s children: anyone who is not righteous is not from God, and neither is anyone who does not love his brother.
For this is the message you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.
Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and killed his brother.
And why did he kill him?
Because his own deeds were evil, and his brother’s were righteous.
Do not be surprised, my brothers and sisters, if the world hates us.
We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brothers and sisters.
Anyone who does not love stays in death.
Anyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life living in him.
This is how we know love: He gave up His life for us. And we ought to give up our lives for our brothers and sisters.
But suppose someone has this world’s goods, and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart against him. How can God’s love live in him?
My little children, let us not love only with words and with our tongue, but with actions and in truth.”

1. Please listen carefully, I beg you, because what we have to deal with is no small matter. And since you were so eager about it yesterday, I have no doubt that you have come together today even more eager.

For it is no small question: how can he say in this letter, “Whoever is born of God does not sin,” when earlier in the same letter he said, “If we say that we have no sin, we are fooling ourselves, and the truth is not in us”?
What should a person do who is squeezed by both sayings from the same letter?
If he admits that he is a sinner, he is afraid someone will tell him, “Then you are not born of God, because it is written, ‘Whoever is born of God does not sin.’”
But if he says that he is righteous and has no sin, he gets hit from the other side by the same letter: “If we say that we have no sin, we are fooling ourselves, and the truth is not in us.”
So he is stuck in the middle. He cannot figure out what to say, what to admit, or what to claim.
Claiming to be without sin is very dangerous. And it is not only dangerous but also wrong. “We are fooling ourselves,” he says, “and the truth is not in us, if we say that we have no sin.”
Oh, if only you had no sin and said so! Then you would be telling the truth. And by speaking the truth, you would have not even a trace of wrong to be afraid of.
But the reason you do wrong when you say it is that what you are saying is a lie.
“The truth,” he says, “is not in us, if we say that we have no sin.”
He does not say, “We have not had sin.” Otherwise it might seem he was talking about our past life.
For a person here has had sins. But since the time he was born of God, he has begun to be without sins.
If that were what he meant, there would be no question to puzzle us.
For we would say, “We used to be sinners, but now we are made right with God. We used to have sin, but now we have none.”
But he does not say this. So what does he say?
“If we say that we have no sin, we are fooling ourselves, and the truth is not in us.”
And then a little later he says the opposite: “Whoever is born of God does not sin.”
Was John himself not born of God?

You have heard that John leaned against the Lord’s chest. If John was not born of God, does anyone dare to promise himself that he has received the new birth that was not given to that man—the man who was allowed to lean against the Lord’s chest?
The man the Lord loved more than all the others—was he the only one the Lord had not given new birth by the Spirit?
2. Now pay attention to these words.

I am still pressing this on you: see what a tight spot we are in. So stretch your minds—that is, pray for us and for yourselves—so that God may make room for us and show us a way out. We do not want anyone to find in God's word a reason for his own ruin. That word was preached and written down only to heal and to save.
“Everyone who sins,” John says, “also does wickedness.”
In case you try to draw a line between the two: “Sin is wickedness.”
In case you say, “I am a sinner, but I do not do wickedness”: “Sin is wickedness.
And you know that He appeared for this reason: to take away sin. And there is no sin in Him.”
And how does it help us that He came without sin?
“Everyone who does not sin stays in Him. And everyone who sins has not seen Him and has not known Him.
Little children, do not let anyone lead you astray.
The person who does what is right is righteous, just as He is righteous.”
We have already said this: the word “as” is usually used to show a kind of likeness, not that two things are equal.
“The person who sins belongs to the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning.”
We have also said this already: the devil did not create anyone, and he did not father anyone. But those who copy him are, in a way, born from him.
“The Son of God appeared for this reason: to undo the works of the devil.”
So the One who has no sin is the One who comes to undo (or set loose) sins.

Then comes this: “Everyone who is born of God does not sin. For his seed stays in him. He cannot sin, because he is born of God.” He has pulled the rope tight! Perhaps he means one particular sin when he says, “does not sin,” and not every sin. So when he says, “Whoever is born of God does not sin,” you can take it to mean one special sin that a person born of God cannot commit. And this sin is the kind that, if someone commits it, it locks all the other sins in place.
What is this sin?
Going against the commandment.
What is the commandment?
“I give you a new commandment: love one another.”
Pay close attention! This commandment of Christ is called “love.”
Through this love, sins are undone.
If this love is not kept, then failing to hold on to it is a serious sin. It is also the root of all other sins.
3. Pay close attention, brothers and sisters. We have put forward something that solves the question for those who understand well.
But should we only walk along the road with those who run faster?
Those who walk more slowly must not be left behind.
Let us turn the matter over from every side, using whatever words we can, so that everyone can reach it.

For I think, brothers and sisters, that a person cares about his own soul if he does not come to church for no reason. He does not look for things that pass away in the Church. He does not come here to do worldly business. He comes here to take hold of something eternal that has been promised to him, something he can reach. Such a person has to think about how to walk on the road. He does not want to be left behind, or turn back, or wander off, or limp and never arrive.
So whoever is serious about this—whether he is slow or fast—must not leave the road.

So this is what I have said. When John says, “Whoever is born of God does not sin,” he probably meant one particular sin. Otherwise it would go against this other passage: “If we say that we have no sin, we fool ourselves, and the truth is not in us.”
So that is how the question can be solved.
There is a certain sin that a person born of God cannot commit. When this sin is not committed, other sins are undone. When it is committed, other sins are locked in place.
What is this sin?
Going against the commandment of Christ, against the New Testament.
What is the new commandment?
“I give you a new commandment: love one another.”

If someone goes against love, and against love for his brother, he should not dare to boast and say that he is born of God. But if someone lives in love for his brother, there are certain sins he cannot commit. Above all, he cannot hate his brother.
And what about his other sins? About those it is said, “If we say that we have no sin, we fool ourselves, and the truth is not in us.”
Let him listen to another place in Scripture that will put his mind at rest: “Love covers a great many sins.”
4. So we praise love, and this letter praises love.
After the Lord rose from the dead, what question did He ask Peter? Only this: “Do you love Me?”
Asking once was not enough. The second time He asked no other question. The third time, no other question either.

When it came to the third time, Peter was hurt. He did not understand the point of it, and it seemed as if the Lord did not believe him. Still, the Lord asked this question a first time, a second time, and a third time.
Three times fear denied; three times love confessed.
Look, Peter loves the Lord.
What should he do for the Lord?
Do not think that the writer of the Psalm did not also feel unsure about what to do: “What can I give back to the Lord for all the good things He has done for me?”
The one who said this in the Psalm noticed what great things God had done for him. He looked for something to give back to God, and he could find nothing.
For whatever you want to give back, you first received from Him, so that you could give it.
So what did he find to offer in return?
As we said, my brothers and sisters, the only thing he found to offer back was what he had received from God.
“I will receive the cup of salvation, and call on the name of the Lord.”
For who had given him the cup of salvation? Only the One he wanted to give something back to.

Now, to receive the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord means to be filled with love. It means being so full of love that you will not only not hate your brother, but you will be ready to die for your brother.
This is perfect love: to be ready to die for your brother.
The Lord showed this in Himself. He died for all. He prayed for the very people who crucified Him, saying, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”
But if He were the only one who did this, He would not be a Teacher, since He would have no disciples.
Disciples who came after Him have done this too.
People were throwing stones at Stephen. He knelt down and said, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
He loved the people who were killing him, because he was dying for them too.
Listen also to the apostle Paul: “And I myself,” he says, “will be used up for your souls.”
For Paul was one of the people Stephen asked God to forgive as he was dying at their hands.
So this is perfect love.
If someone has so much love that he is ready even to die for his brothers and sisters, love is perfect in that person.
But is love already completely perfect the moment it is born?
It is born so that it can become perfect. Once it is born, it is fed. Once it is fed, it grows strong. Once it is strong, it is made perfect. And when it has become perfect, what does it say?
“For me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
I wanted to leave this life and be with Christ, which is far better. But for your sake it is necessary that I stay in the body.”
He was willing to live for the sake of the same people he was ready to die for.
5. You should know that this perfect love is what a person born of God does not break and does not sin against. That is why the Lord says to Peter, “Peter, do you love Me?”
And he answers, “I love You.”
The Lord does not say, “If you love Me, be kind to Me.”

When the Lord lived in a mortal body, He got hungry and thirsty. At that time, when He was hungry and thirsty, people welcomed Him as a guest. Those who had money took care of Him with what they owned, as we read in the Gospel.
Zacchaeus welcomed Him as a guest. By welcoming the Doctor, he was healed of his disease.
What disease? The disease of greed.
For he was very rich, and he was the chief of the tax collectors.
Look at this man, healed from the disease of greed: “I give half of what I own to the poor. And if I have taken anything from anyone, I will pay him back four times as much.”
He kept the other half, not to enjoy it, but to pay his debts.

So at that time he welcomed the Doctor as his guest. He could do this because the Lord had a weak human body, and people could show Him this kindness. And the Lord allowed it because He wanted to give this very gift to those who served Him kindly. The good of it went to those who served, not to Him.
For how could He, whom angels served, need these people's kindness?

Even His servant Elijah did not need this. Once God sent him bread and meat by ravens. And yet, so that a godly widow might be blessed, God's servant was sent to her. The man whom God had fed in secret was fed by the widow.

Still, those who care for the needs of these servants of God do good to themselves. They gain the reward the Lord clearly described in the Gospel: “Whoever welcomes a righteous person because he is righteous will receive a righteous person's reward. Whoever welcomes a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet's reward. And whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is a disciple—I tell you the truth, he will certainly not lose his reward.” So those who do this do it for their own good. But when the Lord was about to go up into heaven, this kind of service could no longer be done for Him.
So what could Peter, who loved Him, give back to Him?
Listen: “Feed My sheep.” In other words: do for your brothers and sisters what I have done for you.
I bought everyone back with My blood. Do not hold back from dying for confessing the truth, so that the others may follow your example.
6. But this, as we have said, brothers and sisters, is perfect love.
The person who is born of God has it.
Pay attention, my dear friends. See what I am saying.
Look, a person has received the sacrament of that birth by being baptized. He has the sacrament—a great sacrament, divine and holy, beyond words.
Think what a sacrament that is!
It makes him a new person by forgiving all his sins!

Even so, he should look closely at his heart. He should check whether what was done to his body has truly been done in his heart too. Let him see whether he has love. Then he can say, “I am born of God.”
But if he does not have love, he may carry the soldier's mark on him, but he is wandering around like a deserter.
Let him have love. Otherwise, he should not say that he is born of God.
But he says, “I have the sacrament.”
Listen to the apostle: “If I know all mysteries, and have all faith so that I can move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.”
7. If you remember, we told you this when we began to read this letter: nothing in it is praised as much as love.
Even when it seems to talk about other things, it always finds its way back to love. Whatever it says, it brings it all back to love.
Let us see whether it does that here.
Look: “Whoever is born of God does not sin.”
We ask, “What sin?” If you take it to mean every sin, it goes against this passage: “If we say that we have no sin, we fool ourselves, and the truth is not in us.”

So let John tell us what sin he means. Let him teach us. Otherwise I may have been too quick to say that the sin here is breaking love. I said it because he said earlier, “Whoever hates his brother is in darkness. He walks in darkness and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.”
But maybe he says something in what comes next, and mentions love by name?
See how this long chain of words ends up here and leads out to this.
“Whoever is born of God does not sin, because His seed stays in him.”
The “seed” of God means the word of God. That is why the apostle says, “I became your father through the Gospel.
And he cannot sin, because he is born of God.”
Let him tell us this. Let us see in what way we cannot sin.
“This is how the children of God and the children of the devil are shown for what they are.
Whoever does not do what is right is not from God, and neither is the one who does not love his brother.”
Yes! Now it is clear what he is talking about: “And neither is the one who does not love his brother.”
So love alone makes the difference between the children of God and the children of the devil.

They may all make the sign of the cross of Christ on themselves. They may all answer, “Amen.” They may all sing “Alleluia.” They may all be baptized. They may all come to church. They may all build the walls of churches. But there is no way to tell the children of God from the children of the devil, except by love.
Those who have love are born of God. Those who do not have it are not born of God.
What a powerful sign! What a powerful difference!
Have whatever you want—if this one thing is missing, it does you no good. If you are missing other things, have this, and you have kept the whole law.
“For whoever loves another has kept the whole law,” says the apostle. And, “Love is the fulfilling of the law.”
I believe this is the pearl the merchant in the Gospel was looking for. He “found one pearl, sold everything he had, and bought it.”
This is the precious pearl: Love. Without it, whatever you have does you no good. And if you have only this, it is enough for you.
Now you see by faith. Later you will see with your own eyes.
For if we love now, when we cannot see, how tightly we will hold on to it when we do see!
But what should we practice on?
On love for our brothers and sisters. You might say to me, “I have not seen God.” But can you say to me, “I have not seen a human being”?
Love your brother. For if you love your brother whom you see, you will see God too at the same time. Because you will see Love itself, and God lives inside.
8. “Whoever does not do what is right is not from God, and neither is the one who does not love his brother.”
“For this is the message.” See how he backs it up: “For this is the message we heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.”

He has made it clear to us that this is what he is talking about. Whoever acts against this commandment is caught in that cursed sin. It is the sin that people fall into when they are not born of God.
“Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and killed his brother.
And why did he kill him?
Because his own works were evil, and his brother's were right.”
So where there is envy, there cannot be love for one's brother.
Pay attention, my dear friends. Whoever envies does not love.
The devil's sin is in that person, because the devil threw man down out of envy.
For the devil fell, and he envied the one who was still standing.
He did not want to throw man down so that he himself could stand. He only wanted not to fall alone.
From what John has added here, hold on to this in your mind: envy cannot live inside love.
You have it said plainly where love is praised: “Love does not envy.”
There was no love in Cain. And if there had been no love in Abel, God would not have accepted his sacrifice.

They both brought offerings. One brought crops from the ground, the other brought young animals from the flock. What do you think, brothers and sisters? Did God look down on the crops and love the young animals?

God did not look at the hands; He looked into the heart. When He saw someone offering with love, He paid attention to his sacrifice. When He saw someone offering with envy, He turned His eyes away from his sacrifice.
So by Abel's good works, John means only love. By Cain's evil works, he means only his hatred of his brother.
It was not enough for Cain to hate his brother and envy his good works. Because he would not copy him, he wanted to kill him.
This showed that Cain was a child of the devil. It also showed that Abel was God's righteous one.
So this is how people are told apart, my brothers and sisters.
Do not pay attention to what people say. Look at their deeds and their hearts.
If someone does not do good for his brothers and sisters, he shows what is inside him.
People are proven by their trials.
9. “Do not be surprised, brothers and sisters, if the world hates us.”
Do I have to keep telling you what “the world” means?
It does not mean the sky or the earth, or the things we can see that God made. It means people who love the world.
I know that by saying this so often, I am wearing some of you out. But I do not say it for no reason. Some people could be asked whether I ever said it, and they would not be able to answer.
So even if I have to push it on people, let something stick in the hearts of those who listen.
What is “the world”?

When “the world” is used in a bad sense, it means people who love the world. When the word is used in a good sense, it means heaven and earth, and the works of God that are in them. That is why it says, “And the world was made by Him.”

“The world” can also mean everyone all over the earth. As John himself said, “Not only for our sins does He make peace with God, but for (the sins) of the whole world.” By “the world” he means all the believers spread out across the whole earth.
But in the bad sense, the world means people who love the world.
Those who love the world cannot love their brother.
10. “If the world hates us, we know”—what do we know?—“that we have passed from death to life”—how do we know?
“Because we love our brothers and sisters.”
No one should ask another person. Each one should go back to his own heart. If he finds love for his brother there, he can put his mind at rest, because he has “passed from death to life.”
He is already on the right hand. He should not worry that, for now, his glory is hidden. When the Lord comes, then he will appear in glory.

For he has life in him, but it is still winter. The root is alive, but the branches look dry, so to speak. Inside is the living substance. Inside are the leaves of the trees. Inside are the fruits. But they are waiting for summer.
So then: “We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers and sisters.
Whoever does not love stays in death.”
Brothers and sisters, so that you do not think it is a small thing to hate, or not to love, listen to what comes next: “Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer.”
Well then—if someone thought hating his brother was no big deal, will he also, in his heart, think murder is no big deal?
He does not lift a hand to kill anyone. Yet God already counts him as a murderer. The other person is still alive, and yet this man is already judged as his killer!
“Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life living in him.”

11. “This is how we know love.” He means perfect love, the perfect love we have urged you to take to heart. “This is how we know love: He gave up His life for us. And we ought to give up our lives for our brothers and sisters.”
See, this is where those words came from: “Peter, do you love Me?

Feed My sheep.” He wanted Peter to feed His sheep in such a way that he would give up his life for the sheep. So that you may know this, He said to him right away: “When you were young, you tied your own belt and walked wherever you wanted. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will tie a belt around you and take you where you do not want to go.

He said this,” the Gospel writer says, “to show by what kind of death Peter would bring glory to God.” So the one He had told, “Feed My sheep,” was the same one He taught to give up his life for His sheep.
12. Where does love begin, brothers and sisters?

Listen for a moment. You have heard how far love goes when it is made perfect. Its very goal and its full measure is what the Lord has set before us in the Gospel: “No one has greater love,” He says, “than this: to give up his life for his friends.”

So He has shown us in the Gospel what perfect love is, and here too it is perfect love that is shown to us. But you ask yourselves and say to yourselves, “When will we ever be able to have ‘this’ love?”
Do not give up on yourself too quickly.
Maybe your love has been born but is not yet perfect. Feed it, so that it does not get choked.
But you will say to me, “And how can I know it is there?”
We have heard how far love goes when it is perfect. Now let us hear where it begins.
John goes on to say: “But if someone has this world's goods and sees his brother going hungry, and closes his heart against him, how can the love of God live in him?”
Look—this is where love begins!
If you are not yet up to dying for your brother, be up to giving your money to your brother right now.
Let love touch you deep inside right now. Do it not to show off, but from the very deepest part of mercy. Think of him, since he is in need now.
For if you cannot give your brother what you do not even need, how could you give up your life for your brother?

Your money sits there close to you, and thieves could take it from you. And even if thieves do not take it, you will leave it behind when you die—even if it does not leave you while you are alive. So what will you do with it?

Your brother is hungry. He is in need. Maybe he is anxious and being pressured by someone he owes money to. He is your brother. You were both bought in the same way. One price was paid for you both. You are both rescued by the blood of Christ. So see whether you show mercy, if you have this world's money.
Maybe you say, “What does that have to do with me?
Should I give my money so that he does not have trouble?”
If that is the answer your heart gives you, the love of the Father does not live in you.
If the love of the Father does not live in you, you are not born of God.
How can you boast that you are a Christian?
You have the name, but you do not have the deeds.
But if your actions match your name, let people call you a pagan if they like. Show by what you do that you are a Christian.
For if you do not show you are a Christian by what you do, everyone may still call you a Christian—but what good is the name to you if the real thing is not there?
“But if someone has this world's goods and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart against him, how can the love of God live in him?”
Then he continues: “My little children, let us not love with words or with our tongue, but with actions and in truth.”
13. I think the matter is now clear to you, my brothers and sisters: this great and deeply important secret and mystery.
All of Scripture shows how powerful love is. But I do not know if any other place shows it more fully than this letter.
We ask you and beg you in the Lord: remember what you have heard. And come eagerly to what is still to be said until we finish the letter, and listen to it eagerly.

But open your heart to the good seed. Pull out the thorns, so that what we are planting in you does not get choked. Instead, let the harvest grow. Then the Farmer will be glad and will get the barn ready for you, as for grain—not the fire, as for the useless husks.
“And this is how we know that we belong to the truth, and how we reassure our hearts before Him.
For if our heart thinks badly of us, God is greater than our heart, and He knows everything.
Dear friends, if our heart does not think badly of us, then we can be confident before God.
And whatever we ask for, we will receive from Him, because we keep His commandments and do what pleases Him in His sight.
And this is His commandment: that we believe in the name of His Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, just as He commanded us.
Whoever keeps His commandments will live in Him, and He in that person.
And this is how we know that He lives in us: by the Holy Spirit He has given us.
Dear friends, do not believe every spirit. Test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into this world.

This is how the Spirit of God is recognized: every spirit that openly says that Jesus Christ has come in a human body is from God. And every spirit that does not say that Jesus Christ has come in a human body is not from God. This is the antichrist. You have heard that he would come, and even now he is already in this world.”
1. If you remember, brothers and sisters, yesterday we ended our sermon with this sentence. It surely should have stayed in your heart, and it still should, since it was the last thing you heard.
“My little children, let us not love only with words and with our tongue, but with actions and in truth.”
Then he continues: “And this is how we know that we belong to the truth, and how we reassure our hearts before Him.”
“For if our heart thinks badly of us, God is greater than our heart, and He knows everything.”

He had said, “Let us not love only with words and with our tongue, but with actions and in truth.” So we are asked: by what action, or by what truth, can we recognize someone who loves God, or loves his brother?

Earlier he had said how far love goes when it is made perfect. The Lord says in the Gospel, “No one has greater love than this: to give up his life for his friends.” The apostle had said the same thing: “Just as He gave up His life for us, we also ought to give up our lives for our brothers and sisters.”
This is perfect love, and you cannot find any greater love at all.

But it is not perfect in everyone. And the person in whom it is not yet perfect should not give up hope, if the love that can grow to perfection has already been born. Of course, if it has been born, it must be fed. It must be fed with its own kind of food, and so be brought to its full perfection. So we asked about the start of love—where it begins. And right away we found this: “But if someone has this world's goods and sees his brother in need, and closes his heart against him, how does the love of the Father live in him?”

So here, my brothers and sisters, is where love begins: giving what you have left over to someone who is in need or in any kind of trouble. It means using your extra earthly things to rescue your brother from earthly trouble.
This is where love first starts to rise.

Once it has started like this, feed it with the word of God and with the hope of the life to come. Then you will finally reach perfection: you will be ready to give up your life for your brothers and sisters.
2. But many such things are done by people who are after something else, and who do not love their brothers and sisters. So let us come back to the witness of our conscience.
How can we prove that many such things are done by people who do not love their brothers and sisters?
Think how many people in heresies and splinter groups call themselves martyrs!
They think they are giving up their lives for their brothers and sisters.
If they really gave up their lives for their brothers and sisters, they would not cut themselves off from the whole family of believers.
And again, how many people give away a lot, hand out a lot, just to show off! All they want from it is people's praise and popularity—which is full of hot air and does not last.
Since there are people like this, how can love for our brothers and sisters be proven?
John wanted it to be proven, and he warned us, “My little children, let us not love only with words and with our tongue, but with actions and in truth.” So we ask: by what action? By what truth?
Is there any action more obvious than giving to the poor?
Many people do this to show off, not out of love.
Is there any action greater than dying for your brothers and sisters?
Many people would like others to think they do this too. But they do it to show off and make a name for themselves, not from a heart full of love.

So what is left? The person who truly loves his brother is the one who reassures his own heart before God, where only God can see. He asks his own heart whether he really does this out of love for his brothers and sisters. And his witness is the eye that sees right into the heart, where no human can look.

Think of the apostle Paul. He was ready to die for his brothers and sisters, and said, “I myself will be used up for your souls.” But only God saw this in his heart, not the human beings he was speaking to. So he tells them, “To me it matters very little whether I am judged by you or by any human court.”

The same apostle also shows in one place that these things are often done from empty showing off, not on the solid ground of love. When he praises love, he says, “If I give away everything I own to the poor, and if I hand over my body to be burned, but do not have love, it does me no good.”
Can a person really do these things without love?
Yes. For those who have broken unity are people who do not have love.

Look there, and you will see many giving a lot to the poor. You will see others ready to welcome death, so much so that when no one is persecuting them, they hurl themselves to their death. These people are surely doing this without love.
So let us come back to conscience. The apostle says about it: “For this is what we boast about: the witness of our conscience.”
Let us come back to conscience. The same apostle says about it, “But each person should test his own work. Then he will have something to boast about in himself, and not in someone else.”
So let each of us “test his own work.” Let him see whether it flows from the vein of love. Let him see whether his good works grow like branches from love as their root.

“But each person should test his own work. Then he will have something to boast about in himself, and not in someone else.” That means not when someone else's tongue speaks well of him, but when his own conscience speaks for him.
3. So this is what John is pressing on us here.
“This is how we know that we belong to the truth: when we love with actions and in truth, not only with words and with our tongue. And we reassure our heart before Him.”
What does “before Him” mean?

It means where He sees. That is why the Lord Himself says in the Gospel: “Watch out that you do not do your good deeds in front of people, to be seen by them. Otherwise your Father who is in heaven will give you no reward.”
