Maybe you are suffering this pressure because you are doing what is right. You are suffering it because you will not give false testimony.
I am only speaking as an example.
There are plenty of examples. For “woe to the world because of stumbling blocks.”
For example, some powerful person wants to cover up his robbery and plunder. So he asks you to serve as a false witness.
You refuse. You refuse to swear falsely, so that you do not deny Him who is true.

To keep this short: he is angry, he is powerful, and he oppresses you. Then a friend comes who does not want you in this pressure of trouble, in this bad situation. He says, “Please, do what you are told. What’s the big deal?”
And then perhaps he speaks as Satan spoke to the Lord: “It is written about You, ‘He will give His angels orders concerning You, so that You do not strike Your foot against a stone.’”
Or perhaps this friend of yours sees that you are a Christian. So he wants to use the Law to persuade you to do what he thinks you should do.
“Do what the other man tells you.”
“What? Do what the other man wants.”
“But it is a lie. It is false.”
“Well, haven’t you read, ‘All men are liars’?”
Now he is a “stumbling block.”
He is a friend. What will you do?
He is an eye, he is a hand: “Cut it off and throw it away from you.”
What does “cut it off and throw it away from you” mean?
Do not agree with him.
The members of our body form one unit by agreeing. By agreeing they live. By agreeing they are joined to one another.
Where there is disagreement, there is disease, or a sore.
So he is one of your members. You will love him.
But he is a stumbling block to you. “Cut him off and throw him away from you.”
Do not agree with him. Drive him away from your ears. Maybe he will come back a better man.
5. I say, “Cut him off and throw him away from you.” Maybe this will even correct him. But how will you do it? Answer me: how are you going to do it?
He wanted to use the Law to persuade you to tell a lie.
He said, “Speak.”
Maybe he did not dare to say, “Tell a lie.” Instead he said, “Say what the other man wants.”
You say, “But it is a lie.”
And he makes an excuse for it: “All men are liars.”
Then, my brother, answer him with this: “The mouth that lies kills the soul.”
Notice that what you have heard is no small thing: “The mouth that lies kills the soul.”
You pity me and my condition. You do not want me to be in this bad situation, but you want me to be evil. So what can that powerful enemy who oppresses me do to me?
What can that powerful man do to me? What can he crush?
The flesh. You will say he can crush your body. I admit he may crush it until it is destroyed.
Still, he treats me much more gently than I would treat myself if I told a lie!
He kills my flesh. I kill my soul.
In his power and anger, he kills the body. But “the mouth that lies kills the soul.”
He kills the body. But the body must die anyway, even if no one kills it. The soul, though, that sin does not kill, the truth receives forever.
So keep safe what you can keep safe. And let go of what must be lost sooner or later.
So you have given an answer. But you have not dealt with “All men are liars.”
Answer him on this too. Then he will not think he has said something to persuade you to lie by quoting the Law. He was using the Law to push you against the Law.
For the Law says, “You must not give false testimony.” And the Law also says, “All men are liars.”
So go back to what I said just now, when I described the “meek” man in words as best I could.
The “meek” person is pleased by nothing but God in everything he does well. And in all the evil he suffers, he is not displeased with God.
Someone says, “Lie, because it is written, ‘All men are liars.’” Answer him: I will not lie, because it is written, “The mouth that lies kills the soul.”
I will not lie, because it is written, “You will destroy those who tell lies.”
I will not lie, because it is written, “You must not give false testimony.”
My telling the truth may displease him, and he may harass my body with oppression. But I will listen to my Lord: “Do not be afraid of those who kill the body.”
6. “Then how are all men liars?
What! I suppose you are not a man?”
Answer quickly and truthfully.
“Oh, that I may not be a man, so that I may not be a liar!”
For look: “God looked down from heaven on the children of men, to see if there were any who understood and sought God.
They have all gone off the path. Together they have all become useless. There is no one who does good, not even one.”
Why? Because they wanted to be sons of men.
But He wanted to rescue them from these sins, and to cure, heal and change the sons of men. So “He gave them power to become the sons of God.”
So what is surprising about this? You were men, if we were the sons of men. You were all men, and you were liars, for “All men are liars.”
The grace of God came to you, and “gave you power to become the sons of God.”
Listen to the voice of My Father saying, “I have said, You are gods, and you are all children of the Most High.”
They are men and sons of men. So if they are not children of the Most High, they are liars, for “all men are liars.”

But suppose they are sons of God. Suppose they have been redeemed by the Savior’s grace, bought with His precious Blood, born again of water and the Spirit, and chosen beforehand to inherit heaven. Then they truly are children of God.
And so, in this way, they are gods.
So what would a lie have to do with you?
Adam was only a man. Christ was man and God. God is the Creator of all creation.
Adam was only a man. The Man Christ is the Mediator with God, the Only Son of the Father, the God-man.
Look, you, O man, are far from God, and God is far above man. The God-man placed Himself between them.
Acknowledge Christ, and through Him, as Man, climb up to God.
7. Now we have been reformed. And if my words have been blessed, we are “meek.” So let us “hold on to what we profess without wavering.”
Let us love the law of God, so that we may escape what is written: “Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks.”
Now I want to say a few words about “stumbling blocks,” which fill the world. I want to say how it is that stumbling blocks multiply and pressing troubles abound.
The world is being laid waste. The winepress is being trodden.

Oh, Christians, you heavenly shoot! You are strangers on the earth. You seek a city in heaven, and you long to be with the holy angels. Understand that you have come here on one condition only: that you will soon leave.
You are passing through the world, trying to reach Him who created it.
There are people who love the world. They want to stay in it, but whether they like it or not, they are forced to leave it. Do not let them upset you. Do not let them deceive or mislead you.
These pressing troubles are not stumbling blocks.
Be righteous, and they will only be exercises.
Trouble comes. It will be whatever you choose it to be: either an exercise or a condemnation.
What it becomes depends on what it finds you to be.
Trouble is a fire. Does it find you to be gold? It takes away the dirt. Does it find you to be chaff? It turns it into ashes.
So the pressing troubles that abound are not “stumbling blocks.”
Then what are “stumbling blocks”?
They are the expressions, the words that people say to us, like this:
“Look what Christian times have brought about!” These are the real stumbling blocks.
This is said to you for one purpose: so that if you love the world, you will speak evil against Christ.
And the one who says this to you is your friend and adviser. So he is “your eye.”
The one who says this to you is the one who serves you and shares your work. So he is “your hand.”
The one who says this to you may be the one who supports you and lifts you up from a low position in the world. So he is “your foot.”
Push them all aside, cut them off, throw them all away from you. Do not agree with them.
Answer such people the way the man answered who was advised to give false testimony.

You answer the same way. Someone says to you, “Look, it is in Christian times that there are such pressing troubles, and the whole world is laid waste.” Answer him, “And Christ told me this before it happened.”
8. So why are you upset?
Your heart is shaken by the pressing troubles of the world, just like that boat in which Christ was asleep.
Tell me, you strong-hearted man, what is the reason your heart is upset?
The boat in which Christ is asleep is the heart in which faith is asleep.
What new thing, I ask you, what new thing is being told to you, Christian?
“In Christian times the world is being laid waste. The world is failing.”
Didn’t your Lord tell you the world would be laid waste?
Didn’t your Lord tell you the world would fail?
When the promise was made, you believed it. So why are you upset now, when it is coming true?
So the storm is beating hard against your heart. Watch out for shipwreck. Wake Christ up.
The Apostle says, “that Christ may live in your hearts by faith.”
Christ lives in you by faith.
If faith is present, Christ is present. If faith is awake, Christ is awake. If faith is sleeping, Christ is asleep.
Get up and rouse yourself. Say, “Lord, we are perishing!”
Look at what the Heathen say to us. And what is worse, look at what bad Christians say!
Wake up, O Lord, we are perishing!
Let your faith wake up, and Christ begins to speak to you: “‘Why are you troubled?’
I told you all these things ahead of time.
I foretold them so that when evil things came, you could hope for good things, and so that you would not lose heart in the evil.”
Are you amazed that the world is failing?
Be amazed that the world has grown old.
It is like a man who is born, grows up and grows old.
Old age brings many complaints: coughing, phlegm, weak eyes, irritability and tiredness.
When a man is old, he is full of complaints. In the same way, the world is old, and it is full of troubles.
Is it a small thing that God has done for you? In the world’s old age He has sent Christ to you, so that He may renew you when everything is failing.
Don’t you know that He showed this in the seed of Abraham?
The Apostle says, “The seed of Abraham, which is Christ.
He does not say, ‘And to seeds,’ as if speaking of many, but as of One, ‘And to your seed,’ which is Christ.”
That is why a son was born to Abraham in his old age: because Christ was to come in the old age of this world.
He came when everything was growing old, and He made it new.
The world is something made, created and perishing. So it was already declining toward its fall.
It had to be full of troubles. He came to comfort you in the middle of present troubles, and to promise you everlasting rest.

So do not choose to cling to this old world and refuse to grow young in Christ. He tells you, “The world is perishing, the world is growing old, the world is failing. It is struggling with the heavy breathing of old age.
But do not be afraid: ‘Your youth will be renewed like the eagle’s.’”
9. “Look,” they say, “it is in Christian times that Rome is perishing.”
Perhaps Rome is not perishing. Perhaps she is only being whipped, not completely destroyed. Perhaps she is being corrected, not brought to nothing.
That may be so. Rome will not perish if the Romans do not perish.
And they will not perish if they praise God. They will perish if they speak evil against Him.
For what is Rome, except the Romans?
We are not talking about her wood and stones, her tall free-standing mansions, and all her wide walls.
All of this was made only on the condition that it would fall someday.
When people built it, they laid stone on stone. And when people destroyed it, they removed stone from stone.
People made it. People destroyed it.
Is Rome harmed because people say, “She is falling”?
No, not Rome. Perhaps her builder is.
Then do we harm her builder when we say that Rome, which Romulus built, is falling?
This world itself, which God built, will be burned with fire.
But what people have made does not fall into ruin unless God wills it. And what God has made does not fall unless He wills it.
If the work of people does not fall without God’s will, how can God’s work fall by the will of people?
Yet God made the world as something that would one day fall for you. And so He made you as someone who would one day die.

Man himself is the city’s ornament. Man himself is the city’s inhabitant, ruler and governor. He comes on the condition that he will go. He is born on the condition that he will die. He enters the world on the condition that he will pass away. “Heaven and earth will pass away.” So why be surprised if a single city comes to an end at some time?
And yet perhaps the city’s end has not come now. But one day it will come.
But why is Rome perishing while Christians offer their sacrifices?
Why was her mother Troy burned while the Heathen offered their sacrifices?
The Romans have placed all their hope in their gods. Yes, the Heathen Romans placed their hope in the Roman gods. And those gods moved from the flames of Troy to found Rome.
These very gods of Rome were first the gods of Troy.
Troy was burned, and Aeneas took the gods that were fleeing. Or rather, he himself was fleeing, and he carried away these senseless gods.
The fugitive could carry them, but they could not flee by themselves.
Aeneas came into Italy with these gods, these false gods, and he founded Rome.
It would take too long to go through the whole story. But I want to mention briefly what their own writings say.

One of their writers, whom everyone knows, says this: “As I have heard the story, Rome was first built and lived in by the Trojans. Led by Aeneas, they were wandering about as refugees with no settled home.”
So they had their gods with them. They built Rome in Latium, and there they set up the gods to be worshiped that had been worshiped before in Troy.
Their poet brings in Juno, angry with Aeneas and the fleeing Trojans. She says,

blocks.x:
“A race of wandering slaves that I hate
Sails with a good wind across the Tuscan sea.
They are steering their course to fruitful Italy,
And there they plan new temples for their conquered gods.”

s: When these conquered gods were carried into Italy, did they come as a protecting power, or as a sign of the fall that was coming to them?
So “love the law of God, and nothing will make you stumble.”

We ask you, we beg you, we urge you: be meek. Feel for those who suffer. Bear with the weak. So many strangers, needy people and suffering people have gathered here now. So on this occasion, let your hospitality and good works overflow.
If Christians will just do what Christ commands, then the Heathen will speak evil only to their own harm.
